title: Load a washer rack so its spray arm turns freely, then turn the arm half a turn
instruction: Load the two white jars and the two steel bowls onto the washer rack, each standing upright on the rack floor inside its walls, so the spray arm can turn freely: anything taller than the arm's underside must stand at least 5 mm outside the circle the arm's ends sweep. Then, without moving or touching the load, turn the spray arm round at least half a turn, so its two ends between them pass over the whole circle. Finish with both grippers at least 2 cm clear of the items.
context: Sterile processing technicians (O*NET 31-9093.00, Medical Equipment Preparers) load washer-disinfector racks before instruments are cleaned. The rotating spray arms clean only while they turn: an item standing in an arm's sweep stops it, and that load comes out with soil left on it and has to be run again. Washer operating manuals tell the operator that the spray arms must not be blocked by items that are too tall or that hang through the baskets, and to turn the arms by hand to check that they move; washer inspection checklists include checking that the spray arms spin freely. Short items may go under the arm; tall ones only where its ends cannot reach: here, with fixed holders taking the far corners, only the two near corners. The task is scored on the loaded rack, measured with a ruler, and on a real half turn of the arm with the load let go of and left undisturbed.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Six kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Washer rack, fixed to the table (a stand-in for a washer-disinfector's lower basket): a dark grey stainless-steel floor plate 31.2 x 31.2 cm and 4 mm thick, centred at x 27.0 cm, y 0, its sides parallel to x and y, with four dark grey stainless walls 6 mm thick and 2 cm tall standing on its edges (their tops 2.4 cm above the table); the walls' inner faces are at x 12.0 and 42.0 cm and at y -15.0 and +15.0 cm (30 x 30 cm inside). (2) Holders: two fixed grey stainless boxes 8.5 x 8.5 cm and 5 cm tall standing on the floor plate in its two far corners, against the far wall and a side wall (x 33.5 to 42.0 cm; y 6.5 to 15.0 cm and y -15.0 to -6.5 cm; their tops 5.4 cm above the table), stand-ins for fittings fixed in a real basket. (3) Feed hub: a fixed light grey stainless cylinder 3 cm across standing on the floor plate's centre (x 27.0, y 0), its top 8.4 cm above the table. (4) Spray arm: a light grey hollow aluminium square tube 22 cm long, 2 cm wide and 2 cm tall, 80 g, centred on the hub and turning on it about a vertical axle (light damping, no spring; it stops 355 degrees either way from the start), its underside 8.5 cm and its top 10.5 cm above the table; a red plastic cap 2 x 2 x 0.4 cm sits on top of one end, its centre 10 cm from the axle. It starts along x with the red end forward (that end at x 38.0). The outer corners of its ends and cap sweep a circle 11.05 cm in radius about the hub's axis, 8.5 to 10.9 cm above the table; the holders' inner corners stand inside that circle, 3.1 cm under the arm. (5) Jars: two white polypropylene jars, closed cylinders 5 cm across and 12 cm tall, 100 g each, standing upright on the table at x 18.0, y +28.0 and at x 18.0, y -28.0. (6) Bowls: two silver-grey stainless-steel bowls standing upside down, cylinders 7 cm across and 4 cm tall, 60 g each, on the table at x 40.0, y +30.0 and at x 40.0, y -30.0. On the rack floor a jar's top is 12.4 cm above the table, 3.9 cm above the spray arm's underside; a bowl's top is 4.4 cm above the table, 4.1 cm below it. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer reads the four items, the spray arm's angle and both grippers every control step (20 Hz). An item is loaded when its centre, seen from above, is inside the rack's inner walls, its axis is within 10 degrees of vertical (either end up) and its lowest point is within 5 mm of the rack floor's top (not lying, stacked, on a holder or held up). A jar is clear when its centre is at least 14.05 cm from the hub's axis and its side is at least 11.55 cm from that axis at every height from 8.5 to 10.9 cm above the table (the arm and its cap; the jar's cross-section there taken as a circle of radius 2.5 cm / cos(tilt)): its side 5 mm or more outside the 11.05 cm circle the arm's ends sweep, even if it leans toward the hub. A gripper is on an item when its fingers come within 2 cm of the item's side, horizontally, with its finger tips below the item's top; the fingers are taken as a disc round the point midway between the finger tips, out to a finger's outer corner (1.68 cm shut, 5.85 cm fully open). A load stretch starts on any step on which all four items are loaded, both jars are clear and no gripper is on an item, and lasts until a step on which that is no longer so or any item's centre is more than 10 mm from where it was when the stretch started; a new stretch can start on that same step. A stretch has a clean half turn once the spray arm's angle (its red end's direction, counted on continuously, not modulo a turn) has been 180 degrees or more from its angle at the start of the stretch, either way; turns back and forth do not add up. Score 0 if at the end any item is not loaded or a gripper is on an item. Otherwise: 0.25 if a jar is not clear; 0.5 if both jars are clear and the stretch running at the end has no clean half turn; 1.0 if both jars are clear and the stretch running at the end has a clean half turn. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. So the turn counts only with the load in place, let go of and left as it was turned: a turn made before the last item is let go of, while a gripper is on an item, or before an item was last moved more than 10 mm, counts for nothing. A jar left in the sweep stops the arm or is tipped by it (about 0.27 N at the arm's height tips it): a tipped jar is not loaded, and no turn counts while a jar stands in the sweep. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s with every item still (its path over the last 0.5 s under 5 mm); otherwise it is scored at the run limit. If the grippers cannot be read on a step, their last reading counts (never read: no gripper is on an item). In a real trial: mark circles of 14.05 cm (the jars' centres) and 11.55 cm (their sides, checked at the arm's height with a square) round the axle; when the last hand leaves the load, draw each item's outline on the floor and film the red cap from above. The half turn counts if the cap passes 180 degrees from where it was then with no hand on the load and no item more than 10 mm outside its outline from then to the end; after a touch or a move of more than 10 mm, redraw the outlines once the hands are off and count the cap from there.
fidelity: A fixed tray with low walls stands in for a washer's lower basket, two plain boxes for fittings fixed in it, and a plain bar on a damped vertical axle for its spray arm, at about 0.6 scale: no water, nozzles or bearing friction, and the axle stops 355 degrees either way from the start (a simulator limit; only half a turn is scored). Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Jars and bowls are solid cylinders of the real items' size and weight.
reset_notes: Stand the jars upright and the bowls upside down back on their start spots, and turn the spray arm back along x with its red end forward. The rack, its holders and the hub are fixed; nothing is consumed.
